questions.question: Which of the following Odissi dancers is also a master of percussion instruments like Mridangam, Pakhavaj and Tabla?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Odissi dancers is also a master of percussion instruments like Mridangam, Pakhavaj and Tabla?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kelucharan Mohapatra.

Key Points

  • Kelucharan Mohapatra (8 January 1926 - 7 April 2004) was a legendary Indian classical dancer, guru, and exponent of Odissi dance, who is credited with the revival and popularizing of this classical dance form in the 20th century.
  •  He is the first person to receive the Padma Vibhushan from Odisha.
  • A noted Sanskrit poet of India writes on this Guru: Saango-paanga-subhangi-laasya-madhuram samteerna-nrutyaarnavam, which translates as - "Each fraction of his dancing body leads to paramount sweetness, through miraculous poses and postures. In fact, Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra crossed the ocean of styles.

Additional Information

  • Sujata Mohapatra is an Indian classical dancer and teacher of the Odissi dancing style.​ 
  • Guru Ramani Ranjan Jena had his initial training in dance and music at the age of 11 from a local teacher.
  • Guru Sudhakar Sahoo is 86 and still dances on stage. The oldest Odissi performer in the world today, he also regularly travels across Odisha and even far-off cities like Ahmedabad and New Delhi to teach dance.

questions.question: Pandit Janki Prasad was associated with which of the following Gharanas of Kathak?
questions.questionHtml: Pandit Janki Prasad was associated with which of the following Gharanas of Kathak?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Banaras

Key Points

  • Pandit Janki Prasad was associated with the Banaras Gharana of Kathak.
  • The Banaras Gharana, also known as the Varanasi Gharana, is one of the three main Gharanas of Kathak dance.
  • This Gharana is known for its intricate footwork, graceful movements, and expressive storytelling.
  • It emphasizes the use of hand movements, facial expressions, and body postures to convey emotions and narratives.
  • Pandit Janki Prasad was a prominent figure in this Gharana, contributing significantly to its development and popularity.

Additional Information

  • Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
  • It traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.
  • The three main Gharanas of Kathak are Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras.
  • Each Gharana has its unique style and repertoire, contributing to the richness and diversity of Kathak dance.
  • The Banaras Gharana is particularly noted for its emphasis on the expressiveness and grace of the dance form.

questions.question: Bharati Shivaji and Kanak Rele are exponents of ______.
questions.questionHtml: Bharati Shivaji and Kanak Rele are exponents of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam

Key Points

  • Bharati Shivaji and Kanak Rele are renowned exponents of Mohiniyattam, a classical dance form from Kerala.
  • Mohiniyattam is known for its graceful and gentle movements, often described as the dance of the enchantress.
  • This dance form traditionally involves themes of love and devotion, and its repertoire includes various elements such as the Cholkettu, Varnam, Padam, and Tillana.
  • Bharati Shivaji has been instrumental in the revival of Mohiniyattam and has received numerous awards for her contributions.
  • Kanak Rele is a pioneer in the field of Mohiniyattam and has established the Nalanda Dance Research Centre, which focuses on the research and promotion of Indian classical dance forms.

Additional Information

  • Mohiniyattam is one of the eight classical dance forms of India recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.
  • The name Mohiniyattam derives from 'Mohini', a mythical enchantress avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu, and 'attam', meaning dance.
  • This dance form is characterized by its elegant costumes, typically a white or off-white sari with a gold border, and distinctive jewelry.
  • It is performed mainly by women and is marked by its fluid, feminine movements and subtle facial expressions.

  • Also known as a 100-drums festival. The Wangala dance is performed by men and women dressed in traditional attire, with the men playing the drums and the women dancing to the beats.
  • The Wangala Festival is a harvest celebration dedicated to main deity Saljong, the Sun-god of fertility.
  • Usually observed for two days, but occasionally it lasts up to a week. The "Ragula" ceremony, which takes place on the first day, takes place inside the chief's home. "Kakkat" is the name given to the second day.

questions.question: Bhutia dance is performed in which of the following states?
questions.questionHtml: Bhutia dance is performed in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

Key Points

  • Bhutia dance:-
    • It is an integral part of Bhutia culture, traditionally performed during festivals, celebrations, and community gatherings.
    • These vibrant dances showcase the rich heritage and storytelling traditions of the Bhutia people, an indigenous group inhabiting the Himalayan regions of India, Nepal, and Bhutan.
    • In India, it is performed in Sikkim.
    • Bhutia dances are characterized by their energetic movements, colorful costumes, and lively music. Some of the most popular Bhutia dances include:
      • Denzong-Neh-Na: This lively dance is performed by both men and women and mimics the movements of birds in flight.
      • Ta-Shi-Yang-Ku: This graceful dance is performed by women and depicts the movements of swans gliding across a lake.
      • Tashi Shabdo: This energetic dance is performed by men and showcases their strength and agility.
    • Bhutia dance costumes are elaborate and colorful, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the Bhutia people. Men typically wear long robes and hats, while women wear colorful dresses and jewelry.
    • The music for Bhutia dances is traditionally played on instruments such as drums, flutes, and cymbals. 

Additional Information

  • West Bengal:-
    • It is a state in eastern India known for its rich cultural heritage, vibrant festivals, and stunning natural beauty.
    • The state's capital is Kolkata, formerly known as Calcutta, which is a major commercial and cultural hub.
    • West Bengal is famous for its exquisite handicrafts, delicious cuisine, and renowned literary figures.
    • The state is also home to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
  • Odisha:-
    • It is a state in eastern India known for its ancient temples, breathtaking beaches, and vibrant tribal culture.
    • The state's capital is Bhubaneswar, which is known as the "Temple City of India" for its numerous ancient temples.
    • Odisha is also famous for its rich handloom tradition, exquisite handicrafts, and delicious cuisine.
    • The state is home to the Lingaraj Temple, one of the largest temples in India, and the Konark Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
  • Nagaland:-
    • It is a state in northeastern India known for its lush green hills, colorful festivals, and unique tribal culture.
    • The state's capital is Kohima, which is known as the "Land of the Nagas". Nagaland is famous for its rich biodiversity, vibrant festivals, and traditional crafts.
    • The state is home to the Naga people, who are divided into numerous tribes, each with its own distinct culture, language, and traditions.

questions.question: Which is the first of India's traditional dance to be refashioned as a theatre art and to be exhibited widely both at home and abroad?
questions.questionHtml: Which is the first of India's traditional dance to be refashioned as a theatre art and to be exhibited widely both at home and abroad?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

Key Points

  •  Bharatanatyam is a major form of Indian classical dance that originated in Tamil Nadu.
  • The Natya Shastra by Bharata Muni and Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikeshvara are considered to be the original sources of Bharatanatyam.
  • The dance form is also briefly mentioned in the Kannada text Manasollasa written by Someshwara III.
  • Lord Shiva is considered the god of this dance form.
  • It gives a wonderful cardio workout, improves blood circulation, tones muscles, and is good for bone density as it is a contact exercise.

Additional Information

  • Kuchipudi is indigenous to the state of Andhra Pradesh and differs from the other five classical styles by the inclusion of singing.
  • The Manipuri Dance, also referred to as the Manipuri Raas Leela is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms, originating from the state of Manipur.
  • Kathakali is a major form of classical Indian dance. It is a "story play" genre of art, but one distinguished by the elaborately colourful make-up, costumes, and face masks that the traditionally male actor-dancers wear.

questions.question: Mrinalini Sarabhai is associated with which of these dance forms?
questions.questionHtml: Mrinalini Sarabhai is associated with which of these dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

Key Points

  • Kathakali
    • Kathakali is a classical dance form that originates from Kerala, a state in the southern part of India.
    • It is distinguished by its vibrant costumes, elaborate makeup, and face masks that the performers wear.
    • Kathakali translates to "Story-Play" and is known for its intricate storytelling, detailed gestures, and expressive eye movements.
    • The dance form combines dance, music, drama, and literature into a composite art form, making it unique and complex.
    • Themes of Kathakali are mostly taken from the Indian epics like Mahabharata, Ramayana, and other ancient scriptures.
    • It is performed exclusively by men and involves rigorous physical training to master the art form.
    • The music used in Kathakali is called Sopanam and is sung in the Malayalam language.

Additional Information

  • Kathak

    • This word is derived from Katha (Sanskrit Word).
    • This dance was spread in India during the Bhakti Movement in the 16th-17th centuries.

questions.question: What is known to be ‘ekaharya’, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
questions.questionHtml: What is known to be ‘ekaharya’, where one dancer takes on many roles in a single performance?
questions.solution: Bharatanatyam, a dance form from Tamil Nadu, is known as 'ekaharya,' where a single dancer portrays multiple roles in a performance. Also called Dasiattam, it has been practiced since 1000 CE, particularly at the Brihadeeswara Temple in Thanjavur. The dance is traditionally divided into seven parts: Alarippu, Jatiswaran, Shabda, Varna, Pada, Thillana, and Sloka. Renowned practitioners include Mrinalini Sarabhai and Yamini Krishnamurthy. In contrast, Kathak originated in North India, Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh, and Kathakali from Kerala, each with distinct characteristics and storytelling methods.

questions.question: Who among the following is best known for creating a fusion style of dance by adapting European theatrical techniques to Indian classical dance?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following is best known for creating a fusion style of dance by adapting European theatrical techniques to Indian classical dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Uday Shankar.

Key Points

  • Fusing European theatrical techniques with India's very own classical and folk dance forms, Uday Shankar came up with his own style of dance.
  • After having named the new dance form 'Hi-dance', he later rechristened it and called it 'Creative dance'.
  • Uday Shankar (8 December 1900 – 26 September 1977) was an Indian dancer and choreographer, best known for creating a fusion style of dance.
  • Uday Shankar was the first to bring the concept of modern dance to India with his novel approach and works.

Additional Information

  • Yamini Krishnamurthy:
    • ​One of India's first classical dancers was Yamini Krishnamurthy.
    • She has received training in both Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam, two contrasting dancing styles.
    • She was born in Madanapalle, Andhra Pradesh, on December 20, 1940.
    • At Chennai's Kalakshetra School of Dance, Yamini Krishnamurthy studied Bharatnatyam under Rukmini Devi Arundale.
    • Later, she received training from illustrious teachers like Thanjavur Kittappa Pillai and Kanchipuram Ellappa Pillai.
    • Under the instruction of Vedantam Lakshmi Narayana Shastri, Chinta Krishnamurthy, and Pasumarthy Venugopal Krishna Sharma, she learned Kuchipudi.
  • Gopi Krishna:
    • He was an Indian Kathak dancer, actor, and choreographer.
    • He also studied Bharatnatyam.
    • In 1952, at the age of seventeen, Gopi Krishna became one of the youngest choreographers in Hindi film history.
    • He was hired to choreograph dances for Madhubala in the film Saqi.
  • Sonal Mansing:
    • ​Indian classical dancer and Guru Bharatanatyam and Odissi dancing style.
    • She is a teacher, researcher, choreographer, and social activist.
    • Also Nominated by the President of India to become a Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha.
    • She is the youngest recipient of Padma Bhushan in 1992 and Padma Vibhushan in 2003.

questions.question: Which of the dance was immediately preceded by a practice session called sevakali and undertaken in the precincts of a temple?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the dance was immediately preceded by a practice session called sevakali and undertaken in the precincts of a temple?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

Key Points

  • Kathakali is a classical Indian dance-drama known for its elaborate costumes and makeup.
  • The dance is preceded by a practice session called sevakali, which is undertaken in the precincts of a temple.
  • Sevakali serves as a preparatory ritual to invoke the blessings of the deities before the performance.
  • This practice is unique to Kathakali and is not found in other classical dance forms.

Additional Information

Option Details
Kathak A classical dance form from North India known for its intricate footwork and spins, but does not have a practice session called sevakali.
Odissi A classical dance from Odisha characterized by its fluid movements and sculpturesque poses, but lacks the sevakali practice session.
Kuchipudi A classical dance-drama from Andhra Pradesh known for its graceful movements and strong narrative, but does not include sevakali.

questions.question: Guru Pankaj Charan Das and Guru Debaprasad Das are associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.questionHtml: Guru Pankaj Charan Das and Guru Debaprasad Das are associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Odissi.

Key Points

  • Odissi is one of the classical dance forms of India originating from the state of Odisha.
  • Guru Pankaj Charan Das and Guru Debaprasad Das were pioneering figures in the revival and popularization of Odissi dance in the mid-20th century.
  • Odissi dance is characterized by its fluid movements, sculpturesque poses, and its emphasis on expressions and gestures (abhinaya).
  • This dance form is traditionally performed to the classical Odissi music, which is a combination of Hindustani and Carnatic music styles.

Additional Information

  • Manipuri
    • Manipuri is a classical dance form from the northeastern state of Manipur.
    • It is known for its graceful and fluid movements, often depicting the Raas Leela (divine love story of Radha and Krishna).
    • The dance form incorporates themes from Vaishnavism and regional deities.
    • Musical accompaniment includes traditional Manipuri instruments like the pung (drum) and pena (string instrument).
  • Kathak
    • Kathak is one of the major classical dance forms of India, originating from North India.
    • It is characterized by intricate footwork, spins, and expressive gestures and storytelling (katha).
    • Kathak dance has both Hindu and Muslim cultural influences and is performed to Hindustani classical music.
    • The dance form developed through the courts of the Mughal emperors and the Hindu temples.
  • Kathakali
    • Kathakali is a traditional dance-drama form from the southwestern state of Kerala.
    • It is known for its elaborate costumes, detailed makeup, and intricate facial expressions and gestures (mudras).
    • The themes of Kathakali performances are usually based on Hindu epics such as the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
    • The musical accompaniment includes traditional Kerala instruments like chenda (drum) and maddalam (drum).

questions.question: Who among the following dancers was the first Odissi dancer of foreign origin to be conferred the Padma Shri in 2006?

questions.question: The Vaishnava saint, Sankaradeva introduced the ______ dance in the 15 th century CE.
questions.questionHtml: The Vaishnava saint, Sankaradeva introduced the ______ dance in the 15th century CE.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sattriya

Key Points

  • Sattriya is a classical Indian dance that originated in the eastern state of Assam. It was recognised as a classical dance by Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.
  • The modern form of Sattriya is attributed to the 15th-century Sankaradeva, who systematized the dance using the ancient texts, and introduced drama and expressive dancing (nritta and nritya) as a form of a community religious art for emotional devotion to Krishna.

Additional Information

  • The Manipuri Dance also referred to as the Manipuri Raas Leela, is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms, originating from the state of Manipur. The dance form is imbued with the devotional themes of Madhura Raas of Radha-Krishna.
  • Odissi, also referred to as Orissi in old literature, is a major ancient Indian classical dance that originated in the temples of Odisha – an eastern coastal state of India
  • Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance. It is the classical dance form of Uttar Pradesh. The origin of Kathak is traditionally attributed to the traveling bards in ancient northern India known as Kathakars or storytellers.

questions.question: Which of the following dance form is wedded with Hindustani music school?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following dance form is wedded with Hindustani music school?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is KathakKey Points

  •  Kathak is the classical dance form that is associated with Hindustani music: 
  • Kathak is the only classical dance form that is associated with Hindustani or North Indian music.
  • It is often performed with the accompaniment of tabla, sitar, and sarangi. 
  • Kathak originated in Uttar Pradesh, North India. It has roots in the Mughal era. 
  • Kathak is usually performed as a solo, with the dancer narrating stories from ancient scriptures through rhythmic footwork, hand gestures, facial expressions, and eye work. 
  • Schools
  • There are three main schools of Kathak, or Gharanas, which are the Jaipur Gharana, the Benaras Gharana, and the Lucknow Gharana.
  • These schools differ in their emphasis on footwork versus acting. 
  • Costumes
  • Hindu female dancers wear a long pleated kurta over pajamas or a sari with traditional jewelry.

questions.question: Who among the following was regarded as the Father of Modern Dance, in India?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was regarded as the Father of Modern Dance, in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Uday ShankarKey Points

  •  Uday Shankar is regarded as the Father of Modern Dance in India.
  • Uday Shankar was an Indian dancer and choreographer
  • He fused European theatrical techniques with Indian classical dance to create a unique style.
  • His dance innovation influenced India, Europe, and the US in the 1920s and 1930s.
  •  In 1938, Uday Shankar founded the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre in Almora, Uttaranchal (now Uttarakhand).
  • Together with his brother, the sitarist Ravi Shankar, he explored classical and folk dance 
  • In 1962, he was awarded by Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance and Drama.
  • In 1971, the Govt. of India, awarded him its second highest civilian award the Padma Vibhushan.

Additional Information

  •  Pankaj Charan Das
    • ​Pankaj Charan Das was a renowned Odissi dancer, choreographer, and teacher 
    • He played a significant role in the revival and popularization of Odissi during the 20th century.'.
    • He received Padma Shri, Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Dance - Odissi.
  • Kunchu Kurup
    • Kunchu Kurup is widely recognised for the dance form of Kathakali
    • It originates from the southern Indian state of Kerala.
    • The dance form is characterised by elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, and exaggerated facial expressions and gestures.
  • Raja Reddy​
    • Raja  Reddy is an Indian Kuchipudi dancer, guru and choreographer
    • They founded and run the Natya Tarangini Institute of Kuchipudi Dance in New Delhi.
    • For their services to the field of arts, the Government of India has conferred on them the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan awards.
    • Kuchipudi is indigenous to the state of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: Who among the following recipients of Kalidas Samman is associated with Classical Dance?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following recipients of Kalidas Samman is associated with Classical Dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sonal Mansingh.

Key Points

  • Sonal Mansingh is a renowned Indian classical dancer and choreographer of Odissi dance style, and she is also proficient in Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi.
  • She has been honored with several prestigious awards including the Padma Bhushan in 1992 and the Padma Vibhushan in 2003 for her contributions to Indian classical dance.
  • Sonal Mansingh has played a pivotal role in popularizing Indian classical dance forms both in India and internationally.
  • She has been actively involved in various cultural and artistic initiatives and has also served as a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of India's Parliament.

Additional Information

  • Kalidas Samman
    • The Kalidas Samman is a prestigious arts award presented annually by the government of Madhya Pradesh in India.
    • It is named after the classical Sanskrit poet Kalidasa and is awarded for outstanding achievement in the fields of classical music, classical dance, theatre, and visual arts.
    • The award includes a cash prize, a citation, and a plaque.
    • Recipients of the Kalidas Samman are selected for their exceptional contribution to the preservation and promotion of Indian art and culture.
  • Jagdish Swaminathan
    • Jagdish Swaminathan was an influential Indian artist and writer known for his contributions to Indian modern art.
    • He was one of the founding members of the Group 1890, an avant-garde group of artists in India.
  • Manna Dey
    • Manna Dey was a legendary Indian playback singer known for his work in Hindi, Bengali, and other Indian languages.
    • He received numerous awards including the Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award.
  • Vilayat Khan
    • Vilayat Khan was a renowned Indian sitar maestro and is considered one of the greatest sitar players of all time.
    • He was awarded the Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan but famously refused both honors.

questions.question: Who among the following was given the title of ‘Queen of Kathak’ by Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was given the title of ‘Queen of Kathak’ by Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sitara Devi.

Key Points

  • Sitara Devi was a renowned Indian classical dancer of the Kathak genre.
  • She was hailed as the Queen of Kathak by the Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore.
  • Sitara Devi's contribution to Kathak has been immense, and she is celebrated for her vibrant and dynamic performances.
  • She has been a recipient of several prestigious awards, including the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Padma Shree.

 Additional Information

  • Kathak is one of the eight major forms of Indian classical dance.
  • The word Kathak is derived from the Vedic Sanskrit word Katha which means "story", and Kathakar which means "the one who tells a story".
  • Kathak dancers tell various stories through their hand movements and extensive footwork, but most importantly through their facial expressions.
  • The dance form traces its origins to the nomadic bards of ancient northern India, known as Kathakars or storytellers.

questions.question: The terms Mahari and Gotipua are associated with which Indian classical dance form?
questions.questionHtml: The terms Mahari and Gotipua are associated with which Indian classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is OdissiKey Points

    • A dancer who performed the Mahari Dance, which is the origin of Odissi.

  • Gotipua
    • A young boy who was dressed as a female to perform the Gotipua dance, which originated as an offshoot of the Mahari tradition.

    • Odissi is one of the eight Indian Classical Dances and is known for its storytelling through movement, expression, and rhythm.

Additional Information

  •  Kuchipudi

    • It is said to manifest earthly elements in the human body.

    • This dance form is from Odisha.

    • This dance form is from Assam.
    • It is governed by strict principles for footwork, music, hasta mudras, and aharyas.

questions.question: For the propagation of which faith was the Sattriya dance form introduced in Assam by Sankaradeva?
questions.questionHtml: For the propagation of which faith was the Sattriya dance form introduced in Assam by Sankaradeva?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vaishnavism.

Key Points

  • Sattriya is a classical dance form from Assam, India.
  • It was introduced by the Assamese saint Sankaradeva in the 15th century.
  • The dance form was created to propagate the teachings of Vaishnavism, a sect of Hinduism that worships Lord Vishnu.
  • Sattriya was traditionally performed in Sattras (Vaishnavite monasteries) as part of religious rituals and ceremonies.

Additional Information

  • Vaishnavism is one of the major traditions within Hinduism, focused on the worship of Lord Vishnu and his avatars, especially Rama and Krishna.
  • Sankaradeva was a 15th-16th century saint-scholar, poet, playwright, and social-religious reformer from Assam.
  • The Sattras are institutions established by Sankaradeva and his disciples to promote the principles of Vaishnavism through various forms of art, including dance, drama, and music.
  • Sattriya dance was recognized as one of the eight classical dance forms of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.
  • Sankari culture, derived from the teachings of Sankaradeva, encompasses a wide range of cultural and artistic expressions, including dance, music, drama, and literature.

questions.question: The actor's performance in a ___________ plays is completely speechless, the story is enacted using a vocabulary of facial expressions and hand-gestures.
questions.questionHtml: The actor's performance in a ___________ plays is completely speechless, the story is enacted using a vocabulary of facial expressions and hand-gestures.
questions.solution: Kathakali is a classical dance-drama from Kerala characterized by speechless performances where the narrative is conveyed through facial expressions and hand gestures. The libretto is sung by singers on stage, accompanied by drummers playing the Chenda. The actors wear elaborate costumes and makeup, enhancing the visual storytelling. In contrast, Bharatanatyam from Tamil Nadu combines pure dance, expressive dance, and dramatic storytelling. Odissi from Odisha features lyrical movements and spiritual themes, while Manipuri from Manipur is known for its graceful movements and Vaishnavite themes, particularly stories of Radha and Krishna.

questions.question: While performing the Suwa folk dance of Chhattisgarh, women act like which of the following birds?
questions.questionHtml: While performing the Suwa folk dance of Chhattisgarh, women act like which of the following birds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Parrot.

  • Sowa or Suwa/Sua tribal dance in Chhattisgarh state is also a form of Parrot Dance.
    • It is a symbolic form of dancing related to the worship of God.
    • Dancers keep a parrot in a pot made of Bamboo and form a circular shape around it.
    • Then performers sing and dance which is a pleasure to watch, moving around it with clapping.
    • This is one of the main dance forms of women of a tribal section of Chhattisgarh.

Additional Information

  •  The Sowa dance songs are an integral part of the heritage, festivals, and celebrations in the rural parts of the state.
    • The performances in this style of song and dance are the special attraction of the celebration of Diwali in the district of Bastar and Soowa or Soowa/Sua tribal dance in Chhattisgarh is also known as Parrot Dance.
    • It is a symbolic form of dancing related to worship.
    • Dancers keep a parrot in a bamboo pot and form a circle around it.
    • Then performers sing and dance, moving around it with clapping. This is one of the main dance forms of tribal women of Chhattisgarh.

questions.question: In 1976, Natya Tarangini, was founded in the National Capital Region, by world renowned Kuchipudi Dance duo ___________.
questions.questionHtml: In 1976, Natya Tarangini, was founded in the National Capital Region, by world renowned Kuchipudi Dance duo ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Radha and Raja Reddy.

Key Points

  • Natya Tarangini, the Kuchipudi dance institution established in 1976 by the famous Kuchipudi duo Drs. Raja-Radha Reddy in Delhi, has nurtured innumerable students over the past decades, as well as their first disciple and the leading exponent Kaushalya Reddy, the Artistic Director of the famed institution today.
  • Kuchipudi is a dance-drama performance, with its roots in the ancient Hindu Sanskrit text of Natya Shastra.
  • Evidence of Kuchipudi's existence in an older version are found in copper inscriptions of the 10th century, and by the 15th century in texts such as the Machupalli Kaifat.
  • The traditional Kuchipudi was performed by a male troupe.

Additional Information

  • Guru Seetha Nagajothy is a reputed Kuchipudi Guru. She was trained in the Gurukul system from the Kuchipudi Maestro Padmabhushan Dr. VempatiChinna Satyam.
  • Dr. Bharativithal and Dr. Vithal, Kuchipudidance couple.
  • Guru Jayarama Rao is known today as one of the foremost Gurus and performers of Kuchipudi style, the vibrant classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, India.​

questions.question: A ______ performance begins with the kelikottu, calling the audience to attention followed by the todayam.
questions.questionHtml: A ______ performance begins with the kelikottu, calling the audience to attention followed by the todayam.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

Key Points

  • Kathakali
    • Kathakali derives its name from the words ‘Katha’ meaning story, and ‘Kali’ meaning drama.
    • It is a wonderful combination of music, dance, and drama.
    • It is presented in the temple precincts after dusk falls.
    • A Kathakali performance is heralded by the Kelikottu or the beating of drums to the accompaniment of the Chengila (gong).
    • It is over 300 years old. 

 Important Points

  • Kathakali
    • Kathakali dance originated in Kerala.
    • It is one of the eight classical dances in India recognised bySangeet Natak Akademi.
    • It is closely related to Koodiyattam (Sanskrit drama tradition) and other ancient martial arts performances also. 
    • Most of the Kathakali recitals are a grand representation of the eternal conflict between good and evil.
    • It draws its themes from the stories narrated in the epics and the Puranas.
      • It is also called the ‘ballad of the east
    • The Indigenous Music of Kerala 'Sopana Sangeetham ' is used in Kathakali.
    • The instruments used in the Kathakali are Chenda (a type of drum), Madhalam (a long cylindrical drum), Chengila ( gong), and Ilathalam (an instrument similar to a cymbal). Sometimes Idakka (a type of small drum) is also used. 
    • Gestures are perhaps the crown jewel of the entire dance drama.
    • Kathakali is remarkable in the representation of the rasas through movements of the eye and eyebrows, through which the story is conveyed.
    • Nine important facial expressions called ‘Navarasas’ are taught to convey different emotions.

Additional Information

  • 8 Classical Dances of India and States: 
Dance State
Bharatanatyam Tamil Nadu
Kathak Uttar Pradesh
Kathakali Kerala.
Kuchipudi Andhra Pradesh.
Odissi Odisha
Sattriya Assam
Manipuri Manipur
Mohiniyattam Kerala

questions.question: Who was recognised as ‘Asthana Nartaki’ (resident dancer) of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam?
questions.questionHtml: Who was recognised as ‘Asthana Nartaki’ (resident  dancer) of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanam?

questions.question: Which of the following dances was traditionally performed by male monks in monasteries?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following dances was traditionally performed by male monks in monasteries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

Key Points

  • Sattriya is a classical dance form of India that originated in the state of Assam.
  • This dance was traditionally performed by male monks in the Vaishnavite monasteries called Sattras.
  • Sattriya dance was introduced in the 15th century by the saint-scholar Sankardev as a medium for religious expression and devotion.
  • The dance is characterized by its spiritual themes, including tales from the life of Lord Krishna and other religious stories.

Additional Information

  • Sankardev:
    • He was a 15th-16th century saint-scholar, poet, playwright, and social-religious reformer in Assam.
    • Sankardev is credited with the creation and propagation of the Neo-Vaishnavite movement in Assam.
  • Sattras:
    • Sattras are Vaishnavite monasteries that were established by Sankardev and his followers to promote the Neo-Vaishnavite culture and religion.
    • These institutions are centers of religious, cultural, and educational activities in Assam.
  • Other Classical Dances of India:
    • Kathakali: A classical dance form from Kerala known for its elaborate costumes and dramatic performances.
    • Kuchipudi: A classical dance from Andhra Pradesh, known for its graceful movements and strong narrative character.
    • Odissi: A classical dance form from Odisha, characterized by its sculpturesque poses and fluid movements.
  • Vaishnavism:
    • It is one of the major traditions within Hinduism that worships Vishnu and his avatars, primarily Rama and Krishna.
    • Vaishnavism emphasizes the devotion (bhakti) towards Vishnu as the Supreme God.
